body: Friday, February 27 2026 — Macro · Sectors · Flows · Crypto

Macro Stance: US growth data is steady and the labour market is not forcing the Fed's hand. Initial jobless claims were 212,000, lower than expected, and the unemployment rate is seen unchanged for February. Fed speakers differ on timing: Goolsbee sees several more cuts this year but not soon, Miran still sees four quarter-point cuts this year, and the odds of early cuts under a Warsh-led Fed have slid. The CBO sees the deficit reaching 5.9% of GDP by 2030, which is the fiscal drag the rate debate has to absorb. Stance: Mixed. The data supports waiting, but the cut path now depends on who runs the Fed and on the deficit.

Rates & Curve: The 2Y closed at 3.42% and the 10Y at 4.02% (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-26), leaving the 10Y-2Y spread at 60 bps and the 10Y-3M spread at 34 bps. The 30Y closed at 4.67% and the 3M at 3.68%, with the 30Y-10Y spread at 65 bps. Over 20 sessions the 10Y is down 24 bps and the 2Y down 14 bps, so the curve is a bull flattening (both down, 10Y down more), and it is moderately steep, approaching the long-run average. Over five sessions the 10Y is down 6 bps. Mortgage rates fell below 6% for the first time since 2022, and Bloomberg reports the same threshold for the 30-year rate. Treasury yields fell as investors awaited more data. The S&P 500 closed at 6,908.86, down 0.54% in the prior session and 0.99% over 20 sessions; the Nasdaq 100 at 25,034.37 is down 3.80% over 20 sessions; the VIX closed at 18.63, up 13.94% over 20 sessions; the DXY at 97.79 is up 1.39% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-26).

New / Most Important: The new fact is that Nvidia fell after a record quarter. A CNBC headline says the blowout report disappointed Wall Street as the stock sank 5%, and the Nasdaq Composite dropped 1.2% as Nvidia pulled tech lower. Nvidia's quarterly profit reached $43 billion, but investors wanted more cash return. The software sell-off is the other half of the story: the WSJ calls it a $1.6 trillion meltdown, and Goldman's prime brokerage says US software stocks will keep rebounding. Bond traders are pricing the risk in duration, with Barron's warning that the tariff ruling could hit bond portfolios.

Playbook ✓: Mixed. Keep a benchmark US equity book but do not chase the index on the Nvidia print. The S&P 500 is caught in an extremely narrow trading range, so breadth needs to confirm any rally. Hold duration rather than cash while the 10Y is 24 bps lower over 20 sessions. Trigger to add risk: a VIX that gives back its 13.94% rise over 20 sessions while the 10Y holds below 4.02%. Trigger to cut risk: a reversal of the 10Y decline that puts the bull flattening into reverse, or a Nasdaq 100 break further below its 20-session level of 3.80% lower.

Macro Stance: European equities closed near records: the STOXX 600 is up 4.29% over 20 sessions at 633.18, the CAC 40 up 6.81% at 8,620.93, the FTSE 100 up 6.64% and the DAX up 4.03% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-26). Engie jumped 7% after a $14 billion UK power grid deal, and a Bloomberg headline says European buybacks are at a record. Stance: Mixed. The equity bid is real, but the trade frame is unsettled: the Reuters explainer asks whether Trump's new surcharge leaves the EU worse off than under the trade deal. European markets closed at record highs on easing tariff fears, but a Bloomberg headline shows a split among Europe's analysts and investors on AI stock swings.

Credit & Inflation: Euro-area food inflation is expected to settle just above 2%, the ECB says, and Lagarde says falling inflation still does not feel real for households. Eurostat's January reading was 1.7%, so the disinflation is progressing but not finished. The ECB sold some dollar assets and cut the weight of the dollar in its reserves, a reserve-diversification signal that matters for the currency. On credit, global spreads widened by the most in months as strains mounted, which is a global signal rather than a Europe-only one.

New / Most Important: The ECB leadership is still the political story. Lagarde again hinted at completing her term, but economists expect her to exit early and hand the job to Knot, and the EU has set a March date for the customs race that Bloomberg frames as a prelude to the ECB tussle. Lagarde's additional BIS salary remains under fire. Merz concluded his China trip saying challenges remain, and the German chancellor's visit leaves Berlin with stronger ties to Beijing even as the Trump trade battle looms. Across the Channel, Reeves' low-key economic update aims to end UK tax chatter, and Revolut is testing a stablecoin in a UK trial, under a regulator that is betting on lighter crypto rules with a stablecoin sandbox.

Playbook ✓: Mixed. Own the European index into a weaker dollar, since the ECB is trimming its dollar reserves and that supports the euro. Trigger to turn Bullish on cyclicals: the EU resuming its vote on the US trade deal with no new US tariff step. Trigger to turn Bearish: a US surcharge that Brussels answers with retaliation. Keep the ECB succession on the watch list, because a change at the top would change the rate path for the second half of the year.

Macro Stance: China's domestic story is holiday consumption and a strong currency, with a stall in internet and AI names. Chinese travellers spent little despite the rise in trips, although jewellery sales surged 33.4% a day during the Spring Festival holiday, per the chamber. Baidu's revenue fell as AI cloud growth failed to offset advertising weakness. Stance: Mixed. The consumption read is positive on volume and weak on value, and the currency is doing more of the work than the domestic economy.

PMIs & Activity: The feed carries no fresh official China manufacturing PMI in the window, so the activity read rests on holiday, retail and corporate data. Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing's earnings show normalisation setting in as stimulus cycles through, and the Hang Seng Tech Index is stuck in a bear market. The Hang Seng itself closed at 26,381.02, down 1.44% in the prior session and down 1.44% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-26). Confirmation would come from the next manufacturing print: a reading that holds above 50 would turn the stance Bullish, while a miss would confirm the stall.

Credit Impulse: The feed has no fresh total social financing print, so the credit impulse cannot be measured from headlines. The policy signal runs through the currency. The PBOC set another stronger fixing, while Beijing is trying to slow the yuan's gains by making it costlier to short the currency. A Reuters commentary argues China must uncap the yuan to win Europe's embrace. Until a TSF print turns positive, we read credit as stable rather than expanding, and the currency is not a substitute for credit.

Property: The price signal is split. Hong Kong home prices reached a 19-month high as the rise gathers pace, with analysts forecasting a 2026 rise of at least 10%. The mainland is different: Shanghai eased residency requirements for homebuyers to spark a recovery, but the supply side is still being managed, with steel mills asked to curb output at a government meeting. Hong Kong is a separate market from the mainland, so the Hong Kong recovery does not show up in mainland property prices.

Fiscal, Policy & Trade: The US is keeping China tariffs steady ahead of a key Trump–Xi meeting, according to Greer, and China has received a major reprieve on tariffs, though no reversal is expected. Beijing's export controls are coming of age as Trump reins in China tech curbs, and China has opened its capital account in Hong Kong gently. Japan is the sharper edge: China's export bans on Japanese firms escalated the pressure on Tokyo. Nvidia still has not sold its US-approved China AI chips and is worried local rivals could take over.

Markets & Flows: The Shanghai Composite closed at 4,146.63, down 0.01% in the prior session and up 0.72% over 20 sessions. ASHR, the CSI 300 tracker, closed at 34.17, up 1.52% over 20 sessions, while FXI fell 2.68% in the session to 37.39 and KWEB fell to 31.46, down 12.83% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-26). USD/CNY closed at 6.8692, down 1.23% over 20 sessions, so the yuan keeps strengthening. Four Hong Kong listings seek $626 million as the market revives after the Lunar New Year, and South Korean investors are pouring millions into Chinese AI and tech stocks.

New / Most Important: The yuan is the new fact. The currency's rally is getting a policy response, with Beijing moving to slow the gains while options traders target 5% gains. Merz left China with stronger ties as the Trump trade battle looms, and the yuan had already picked up ahead of his visit. For investors the question is whether the currency rally can hold through the Trump–Xi meeting without a policy brake.

Playbook ✓: Mixed. Prefer ASHR and broad onshore exposure over KWEB and the Hang Seng Tech. Trigger to turn Bullish: a tariff settlement before the Trump–Xi meeting or a consumption package that the holiday data can fund. Trigger to turn Bearish: a summit that stalls alongside a further escalation in export controls. ⚠ Divergence: the PBOC is leaning against yuan strength while it keeps setting stronger fixings, and the Hang Seng is down 1.44% over 20 sessions despite the currency's rally.

Macro Stance: The BOJ has left the door open to near-term rate hikes, and the yen reclaimed some ground. The yen strengthened after the BOJ signalled data-driven hikes, but the government has put two doves in a row on the board, and it picked reflationists for the board in line with Takaichi's view. Stance: Mixed. The central bank is hawkish in its words and the board is dovish in its votes, and the yen is where that split shows. China is piling pressure on Japan after Takaichi's triumph, and Japan condemned a reported Chinese influence operation aimed at its elections, so the political risk is part of the rate story.

Activity & Currency: Core inflation in Tokyo slowed below the BOJ's 2% target in a test for policy, while the yen touched roughly a two-week low on the board picks and the finance minister signalled greater vigilance over yen weakness. USD/JPY closed at 156.2000, up 2.03% over 20 sessions, and the Nikkei 225 closed at 58,753.39, up 10.16% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-26), with the index at a new record high. Forecasts for the Nikkei were revised upward after the LDP's big win, and the average new condo price hit a record in 2025, which keeps domestic demand in the story.

Playbook ✓: Mixed: own the Nikkei, which is at a record, but pair it with a yen hedge because the currency is where the policy risk sits. Trigger to turn Bullish on the yen: a BOJ hike in the spring that the board endorses. Trigger to turn Bearish on the yen: a hold with a dovish board majority and USD/JPY moving decisively through its 156.2000 close. Ultra-long JGBs stay a second-order risk until the board votes are clear. Political items to track are the flag-desecration bill and the aid programme due by March, both of which affect the fiscal path that the BOJ must weigh.

Macro Stance: The RBA is on the defensive. The governor says inflation is not taking off again, but the hot inflation figures kept a rate hike on the table, and Bullock says patience is needed as rate calls get tougher. The March decision is a live risk after the inflation surprise. Stance: Mixed, with a tightening bias: the domestic rate path leans hawkish while the currency and the stock market are still rising. The opposition is part of the story as well: Tim Wilson's RBA comments are making waves, and he walked back a suggestion that the Liberals would rethink the RBA's full-employment mandate.

Demand & Financing: AUD/USD closed at 0.7120, up 1.15% over 20 sessions, and the ASX 200 at 9,175.30, up 2.33% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-26). Carry-trade demand is lifting the currency. Lenders are passing the cycle on, with Westpac and CBA raising fixed rates in a warning to borrowers. WiseTech will cut 2,000 jobs as AI ends manual coding, and investors are weighing whether the AI-driven cuts and steady guidance change the case for the stock. Qantas posted record earnings, and Chalmers is eyeing a budget upgrade as gold eclipses gas exports. Wages are the live issue: Australia's high wage growth reinforces the RBA's inflation challenge, and workers are going backwards as wage growth lags inflation over the past year. The AI job-cut debate is also in the mix, with a Block headline arguing an AI job doom loop is not here yet.

Playbook ✓: Mixed. Hold the ASX 200 with a bias towards banks, which benefit from a hike, and keep the AUD exposure hedged around the March decision. Trigger to add: a March hike that is not followed by a pause. Trigger to cut: a core inflation print that falls back, which would take the May-hike bet off the table. Watch the unemployment rate of 4.1% against the hike talk: a jobs print that weakens would make the May-hike bet harder to sustain.

Monetary & Activity: The monetary council decides on rates, and the decision will be felt beyond borrowers. The economy is speeding up while the labour market cools, and the EBRD expects Polish growth of 3.7% this year. The budget is the weak link: revenues for 2025 came in nearly 30 billion lower while state spending grew, and the Commission warns that debt will breach 100% of GDP by 2036. Housing is turning: Poland saw its first annual house-price fall since 2013, and 90 thousand mortgages left bank portfolios as variable rates gained, even as new mortgage lending rose 32%.

FX & Markets: USD/PLN closed at 3.5654, down 0.38% in the prior session and up 1.59% over 20 sessions, and EUR/PLN at 4.2122, up 0.21% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-26). EPOL closed at 38.19, down 1.34% in the session, while the Beta ETF WIG20TR at 68.59 is up 1.99% over 20 sessions. Named stocks: KGHM closed at 321.80, down 5.91% in the session after a 7.63% gain over five sessions; PKN Orlen at 115.24, up 8.23% over 20 sessions; PKO BP at 93.60, up 3.06%; PGE at 11.09, up 16.30%; PZU at 67.54, down 2.60% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-26). The zloty is stable against the franc.

Companies: Orlen plans to inject 5.1 billion zloty into utility Energa, and its gas-bill change is one of the few household-facing moves in the state champion's plan. KGHM has a new CEO and a wage agreement with unions. Chemical maker Azoty seeks an 83% debt writedown in its polymer restructuring. The regulator is active too: the competition watchdog searched Allegro's offices in Poznań and Warsaw, and PKO BP had a large outage that customers reported before service was restored.

Security & New Development: Security policy is now a market story. Poland withdrew from the treaty banning anti-personnel mines, and five countries will develop low-cost air-defence systems together. Poland ended the special status of Ukrainian refugees, and nearly one million Ukrainian refugees are in Poland after four years of war. Foreign Minister Sikorski says Poland is a loyal US ally but cannot be a 'sucker'.

Playbook ✓: Mixed: own the state-linked cash generators, KGHM and Orlen, for the commodity and dividend tailwind; avoid domestic-demand names until labour and budget data turn; and treat the zloty's 1.59% gain on the dollar as a hedge cost rather than a trend. Trigger to turn Bullish on domestic names: a rate decision that signals cuts without a further labour slide. Trigger to turn Bearish: a further revenue shortfall in the budget. ⚠ Divergence: state-linked names rose strongly over 20 sessions, with PGE up 16.30% and PKN up 8.23%, while the budget revenue came in nearly 30 billion lower and the labour market is cooling.

Narrative: Technology is split between AI hardware and AI software. XLK closed at 141.01, down 1.40% in the prior session and 5.51% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-26). The software sell-off is the driver: the WSJ calls it a $1.6 trillion meltdown, while AI is now seen as saving some software names.

Reported: Nvidia's blowout quarter disappointed Wall Street and the stock sank 5%, with investors wanting more cash return. Salesforce's record $50 billion buyback is controversial with Wall Street, and Intuit's guidance missed estimates.

EPS Upside Watch: Dell expects AI server revenue to double in fiscal 2027, the one hardware forward signal in the feed. The headwind is cost: the smartphone market is set for its biggest-ever decline in 2026 on a memory price surge, which also squeezes PC makers.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Nvidia's record quarter got a sell-off while Goldman's prime brokerage expects US software stocks to keep rebounding. The AI-hardware and software-rebound trades are working against each other, which breaks the single AI consensus.

Narrative: Communication services is a mix of ad platforms and streaming. XLC is flat over 20 sessions at 116.72 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-26). Alphabet is down 8.52% over 20 sessions at 307.38, while Meta is down 1.75% at 657.01 and Netflix is up 9.86% over five sessions at 84.59.
Reported: Warner Bros. Discovery missed Q4 estimates and revenues fell year on year. Zoom posted a rare quarterly earnings miss, although its fundamentals remain strong.

EPS Upside Watch: Meta signed a multi-billion-dollar deal to rent Google AI chips, so platform compute is being sourced across rivals. The feed carries no preview headline for the other platform names in the card.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Meta renting Google's AI chips is a sign that platform capex is spreading across vendors. That cuts against the single-winner consensus in AI hardware and is a reason the platform names are not yet rallying with Nvidia.

Narrative: Financials are mixed. XLF is up 1.21% in the prior session but down 0.92% over 20 sessions at 52.50 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-26). Private-credit stress is the drag: Apollo's private-credit fund marked down its portfolio on soured loans, and FS KKR's private-credit fund cut its dividend amid rising bad loans.

Reported: RBC beat profit estimates on personal banking and wealth management, with a $5.79 billion first-quarter profit. TD reported a $4.04 billion Q1 profit, up from $2.79 billion a year earlier, and CIBC posted record revenue across its divisions.

EPS Upside Watch: Canadian banks are the beat-and-hold set-up. The feed says big Canadian banks beat profit estimates as the economy resists the tariff impact, and wealth and trading lines are the drivers. Those lines are the most likely to beat again.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Private-credit stress keeps landing on lenders' balance sheets. Marathon's Richards fears 15% direct-loan software defaults, and Bain Capital's Rufino warns the software default rate could hit double digits. Bank beats do not offset that.

Narrative: Energy has been the strongest sector over 20 sessions: XLE is up 9.99% at 55.05 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-26), while Brent closed at 70.75 and WTI at 65.21. Oil settled down after a choppy session as traders followed the US–Iran talks, and a Reuters commentary says geopolitical turmoil gives OPEC+ cover for a cautious output hike.

Reported: Alberta projects a C$9.4 billion deficit on lower oil prices, a sign of the price drag on producers. Trump pushed for lower gas prices and got them, and the oil industry is paying the price.

EPS Upside Watch: The energy earnings set-up is price-sensitive rather than volume-driven. The falling gasoline price and the provincial deficit point to producers facing the price drop, so upside sits with hedged producers that have cash-return plans.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Energy is rallying over 20 sessions while the policy push is for lower pump prices. A policy that works against the sector's price is the convention breaker: the sector is up on Iran risk while the administration is pushing prices down.

Narrative: Industrials are in a capex cycle. XLI is up 7.65% over 20 sessions at 176.70 and up 0.63% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-26). Power and grid equipment are the engine, with GE up 16.53% over 20 sessions at 340.84.

Reported: Schneider Electric rose after earnings as AI data-centre growth drove its outlook, and Rolls-Royce shares popped as profits jumped nearly 40%. Engie jumped 7% after a $14 billion UK grid deal.

EPS Upside Watch: The set-up is data-centre power equipment and grid build-out. Schneider's AI data-centre outlook is the forward line to watch, and the grid deals show the capex is moving from plans to contracts.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The White House data-centre power deal is short on specifics: Trump's deal is still unclear in its detail, and Georgia's Senate blocked a vote on a data-centre energy bill. Industrials gain from the build-out only if the rules become clear.

Narrative: Consumer discretionary is weak on the card: XLY is down 3.88% over 20 sessions at 117.05, Amazon is down 14.44% over 20 sessions at 207.92 and Tesla is down 5.30% at 408.58 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-26). Tesla's China problem keeps getting worse in Europe, and China's carmakers are ceding ground in Europe.

Reported: Shake Shack's earnings explosion sent its shares soaring, but Sweetgreen's $5 billion stock wipeout followed soggy fries and lettuce shortages. Hertz is buying Dollar Thrifty for about $2.3 billion.
EPS Upside Watch: The beats that work are the ones with a sales lift and a clear traffic story, as Shake Shack's rally shows. Discretionary names without a forward raise are not the EPS set-up.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Hertz's purchase of Dollar Thrifty is a consolidation bet in a sector the card shows falling. Deal activity is supporting the rental names while the discretionary tape is weak, which is the reverse of the consumer-spending narrative.

Narrative: Staples are the defensive winner over 20 sessions: XLP is up 7.94% at 88.86 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-26), and Walmart is up 6.73% over the same window at 124.42. The driver is rotation out of AI-exposed growth and into cash-generating names.
Reported: Diageo's share price crashed after its dividend cut, and the question is whether it is a buy, a hold or a sell. Hormel missed quarterly sales estimates on weak retail demand.

EPS Upside Watch: The feed has no preview headline for the staples names in the card. The EPS upside sits with the staples that can hold price and volume, and the Hormel miss shows that volume is the test.
⚡ Breaking Convention: Staples are up while Diageo's dividend cut and Hormel's sales miss show defensive names are not immune to weaker volumes. The defensive label is the weak point of the trade.

Narrative: Healthcare is mixed: XLV is up 2.02% over 20 sessions at 157.42 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-26). The policy overhang is drug pricing: Politico asks whether the drug-pricing hurdle can be cleared, and TrumpRx savings for the insured are limited by US discount laws.
Reported: Hikma's gloomy outlook sent its shares to a more-than-three-year low. The Justice Department backs AbbVie in its bid to overturn a Colorado law guiding drug discounts.

EPS Upside Watch: The drug-pricing rules are the main earnings driver in the feed, so the EPS upside is in names with little US price exposure. The feed carries no positive preview for the large caps in the card.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Lilly is down 0.17% over 20 sessions at 1,022.02, yet the TrumpRx headline shows that enforcement of the pricing push is limited. The convention that price cuts hurt the leader is being tested by the limits on the policy itself.

Narrative: Materials are a commodity-leverage trade: XLB is up 6.11% over 20 sessions at 53.00 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-26). Gold closed at 5,194.20, down 2.06% over 20 sessions after a 3.94% gain over five sessions, while silver at 87.00 is down 23.09% over 20 sessions. JPMorgan sees gold at $6,300 by the end of the year.

Reported: Lynas profit jumped as geopolitics 'reshape' the rare-earths market, and Lynas is cashing in on Trump's critical-minerals drive. Copper's rally has run into a wall: copper edged lower as traders await China demand.

EPS Upside Watch: The EPS set-up is producers whose costs stay put while prices rise. Gold miners are the candidates, and the feed shows Gunnison's updated study highlights 3.2 billion pounds of copper production, a long-dated supply story.

⚡ Breaking Convention: China's copper went from investment fad to scrap in a month, so copper's move is about China positioning rather than a growth read. Silver is down over 20 sessions even as the sector is up, which is the convention breaker in the materials trade.

Narrative: Real estate is a rate trade: XLRE is up 6.81% over 20 sessions at 43.63 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-26). Mortgage rates below 6% for the first time since 2022 are the driver, and the relief for US homeowners is widely reported.
Reported: Bloomberg's headline on the 30-year mortgage rate confirms the threshold, and the Hill reports rates below 6% for the first time in more than three years.

EPS Upside Watch: Builders are the EPS watch. Mortgage volume is the question: economists do not expect a housing boom from the lower rate, so the set-up favours builders that can convert rate relief into orders.
⚡ Breaking Convention: Rates are falling but transactions are not following: economists do not expect a housing boom. The sector is priced for rates, while volume is the signal it does not yet have.

Narrative: Utilities are the AI-power trade: XLU is up 8.89% over 20 sessions at 47.18 and Constellation is up 12.37% at 323.56 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-26). The White House is hosting Big Tech after a pledge to rein in power costs, and the data-centre share of US electricity is seen doubling by 2030.
Reported: Vistra reported its fourth-quarter and full-year 2025 results, and Texas approved a data-centre gas power project.
EPS Upside Watch: The capital plans carry the earnings. A new Google data centre triggers 1.9 GW of clean energy, which is demand that regulated and merchant generators can contract against.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The pledge is unclear on what it commits. Politico's headline asks what is in the Trump data-centre deal, and Semafor argues the problem is the data-centre power plan itself. The power trade is priced for a commitment that is still undefined.

Narrative: European autos are the laggard within the rally. The iShares STOXX Europe 600 Automobiles tracker closed at 46.40 in euros, up 2.62% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-26), but Stellantis is down 17.01% over 20 sessions at 8.05. Stellantis posted its first annual loss in its history after EV write-downs.

Reported: Stellantis warned of higher US tariff costs as it reported a €22 billion loss, and the US closed its probe into 7.4 million Stellantis vehicles without seeking a recall. Its shares rose despite the loss.

EPS Upside Watch: The EPS set-up for autos is a turnaround that has to show profit. Stellantis's CEO vows a profit rebound after the EV write-down, and Volkswagen is betting on self-driving to win the growth argument.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Stellantis rose on an annual loss while it weighs using Chinese EV technology for the first time in Europe. The market rewards the turnaround, and the European supply chain is turning toward Chinese technology.

Narrative: Semis lead the AI hardware trade but are in a pullback: SOXX is down 1.02% over 20 sessions at 356.80 and fell 3.04% in the prior session; SMH is at 412.01, down 3.32% in the session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-26). TSMC expects AI chip revenue to grow at a 60% CAGR through 2029.
Reported: Nvidia's stock fell after its record quarter. ASML was down on the day, even as the company says its next-generation EUV tools are ready to mass-produce chips.

EPS Upside Watch: Micron is up 326% in a year, but its shares are 4.53% lower over 20 sessions at 415.56 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-26). The next memory print will show whether pricing carries into earnings; the smartphone market is set to shrink 13% on the memory crisis.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The memory boom is a cost for device makers. IDC says the smartphone market faces its biggest-ever decline in 2026 on a memory price surge. Semis gain from the cost that hurts their customers, and Nvidia's sell-off shows that a strong print is not enough when the forward line is only in line.

Rewarded: Beats with a forward line were paid. LSEG shares jumped as the exchange group forecast a profitability boost and promised $4 billion of buybacks, and Rolls-Royce's profit jumped nearly 40%. IonQ jumped 22% after an earnings beat, with a 2026 revenue outlook above forecasts. Shake Shack's earnings explosion sent its shares soaring. Canadian banks kept topping expectations: TD's quarterly earnings were lifted by growth across operations, and RBC's by personal banking and markets.

Punished: Beats without a forward raise were not. Nvidia sank 5% on a record quarter, Duolingo tumbled 22% on weak guidance and slowing user growth, CoreWeave slid as its quarterly revenue guidance disappointed, and Intuit's guidance missed estimates. Salesforce crushed earnings by 25% and still cannot get any respect. Duolingo's sales topped estimates, yet its stock still dropped 22.5%, which is the same lesson as the guide: the top line is not the test.

Pattern: The guide is the pricing unit, and the beat is already in the price. Names with AI-supply exposure were sold on the forward line: Nvidia fell on returns and CoreWeave on guidance. Names with a profit trajectory rose: LSEG and Rolls-Royce. Salesforce's $50 billion buyback is controversial, which shows that capital return does not rescue a weak forward line. The card's Nvidia move (down 5.46% in the prior session) is the test case for the pattern. Canadian banks show the opposite pattern: a beat that holds, because the personal-banking and wealth lines lift the outlook.

Attention into EPS: The next tests are set up. Snowflake's beat lost steam after results, although its $7.88 billion revenue backlog is impressive. Dell's AI server guide is the next hardware read on whether the forward line holds up. The Nvidia case says the market is looking for more cash return and a lower-risk guide, not just a bigger quarter. Rocket Lab posted a record quarter, and Solventum introduced its 2026 full-year guidance, both of which are the next forward reads for their groups.

Playbook: Own beat-and-raise and profit-trajectory names into the next print. Sell AI-supply names into strength where the forward line is only in line, and avoid software that beats without a raise. Trigger to reverse: a cash-return announcement from Nvidia that answers the investor complaint, which would reset the AI-supply multiple. Size on the guide, not the print, as the Duolingo and Nvidia cases show.

Attention Gap: Attention is on US tariffs and the EU trade deal, but the bigger European story is supply. Stellantis is weighing the use of Chinese EV technology for the first time in Europe, Leapmotor's technology could go into Fiat, Peugeot and Opel cars, and China's carmakers have ceded ground in Europe after surging in 2025.

Exposure & Risk: The exposure is Stellantis, which is down 17.01% over 20 sessions at 8.05 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-26), and the European battery supply chain. Europe's battery dreams clash with China's manufacturing dominance. The risk is that the shift is a loss of European jobs and a policy reversal, not a trade. The competitive shift shows from the other side too: Tesla's China problem keeps getting worse in Europe.
Trigger to Watch: A signed Stellantis deal on Chinese EV technology would make the theme consensus. A policy move to limit Chinese supply in Europe would reverse the thesis.

Attention Gap: Hong Kong's listing revival gets less attention than the mainland stimulus debate. Four Hong Kong listings seek $626 million as the market revives after the Lunar New Year, and China is opening its capital account in Hong Kong gently. Hong Kong's exchange earnings show normalisation setting in. Hong Kong's home prices reached a 19-month high, a property signal that is separate from the mainland.

Exposure & Risk: The exposure is Hong Kong exchanges and the offshore yuan, with the Hang Seng down 1.44% over 20 sessions at 26,381.02 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-26). The risk is that the Hang Seng Tech Index stays in a bear market even as the offshore currency gains.
Trigger to Watch: A formal step on the capital-account opening would make the Hong Kong listing story consensus. Further outflows from the Hang Seng Tech names would confirm the bear market.

Attention Gap: Rare-earth shortages are worsening in US aerospace and chips despite the trade truce, according to sources, and chipmakers are still suffering shortages. The attention goes to Lynas and China, while the US magnet supply is still forming: MP Materials selected Texas for its rare-earth magnet manufacturing site.

Exposure & Risk: Exposure is MP Materials, Lynas, and rare-earth-linked industrial names. Lynas's profit jumped as geopolitics reshapes the market, but the shortage is a supply constraint that can hurt chipmakers' output. The Economist warns that America's critical-mineral dominance is a dangerous pursuit. Japan leans more on China for rare earths despite lower imports, so the US magnet build is a diversification bet as much as a growth one.
Trigger to Watch: The first commercial magnet output from the Texas site would move the theme to consensus. A renewed Chinese export restriction would widen the shortage and the premium.

Attention Gap: The yen is treated as a currency story, but the board split is the under-owned variable. The yen strengthened after the BOJ signalled data-driven hikes, while the government put two doves on the board and picked reflationists. The finance minister's vigilance over yen weakness is the signal the market is still missing.

Exposure & Risk: The exposure is USD/JPY, at 156.2000 with a 2.03% gain over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-26), and yen options. The risk is a dovish board majority that leaves the yen to slide while the Nikkei, at a record, keeps rising.

Trigger to Watch: A BOJ hike in the spring that the board endorses would reprice the yen. A joint or unilateral intervention would show the authorities' limit. Tokyo's core inflation below the BOJ's 2% target is the input the board votes will weigh, so the next inflation print matters more than the speeches.

Market Context: Bitcoin closed at 67,453.77, down 0.81% over five sessions and 4.40% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2026-02-26). Ether closed at 2,026.79, down 1.77% over 20 sessions, and Solana at 85.91, down 1.78%. IBIT closed at 38.26, down 24.25% over 20 sessions, while MSTR closed at 133.40, down 15.81%, and COIN at 181.06, down 13.55%. Bitcoin rode the Nvidia wave above $70,000 before pulling back, and then resumed its slide after a quick pullback in risk appetite. The pullback followed a quick reversal in risk appetite, and analysts are split on whether the rally is a one-day event.

New / Most Important: The stablecoin and institutional plumbing keep building. The GENIUS pitch has cast a dark cloud over the stablecoin model, according to CoinDesk, while Morgan Stanley says it will offer bitcoin custody, trading, yield and lending. JPMorgan sees a crypto boost if the market-structure bill passes. Circle is nearly 50% higher in two sessions since its earnings. Incumbents are moving in: Morgan Stanley's custody plan and Franklin Templeton's bet on tokenised funds are the signals. A US judge also ruled that Binance cannot arbitrate customer claims over crypto losses, which is a legal limit on the exchange model.

Playbook: Mixed. The hurdle is the $70,000 close: Bitcoin spiked above it on the Nvidia wave and failed to hold. Own protection on MSTR and COIN into any squeeze, and buy spot only on a daily close above $70,000. The trigger to turn bearish is another leg of ETF outflows, while BlackRock's dominance of the bitcoin ETF landscape is the sign that flows are concentrating rather than leaving. Options positioning matters: $8.8 billion of BTC and ETH contracts could trigger volatility, and an inverse bitcoin product popped 25%, so the squeeze risk runs both ways.

Global Liquidity: A Seeking Alpha headline says a $137 billion liquidity drain has begun and may mean trouble for stocks. The ECB sold some dollar assets and cut the weight of the dollar in its reserves. Hong Kong's shock move to tap its dollar defence fund fuels concern, while the Philippine peso is set for its best start in 14 years on stock inflows and a weak dollar. Money managers are favouring emerging markets, Citi says, and the EBRD says the Trump tariff turmoil has not dented emerging-market growth.

Rates & Dollar: The 10Y is 4.02% and the 2Y 3.42% (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-26), a bull flattening over 20 sessions with the 10Y 24 bps lower. The DXY at 97.79 is up 1.39% over 20 sessions. Barron's warns the tariff ruling could hit bond portfolios, and Bloomberg says the Trump agenda needs allies to stick with Treasuries as the rest flee. TLT closed at 90.27, up 3.05% over 20 sessions, and IEF at 97.60, up 1.77% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-26).

Credit Check: Global credit spreads widened by the most in months as strains mount. Bain Capital's Rufino warns the software default rate could hit double digits, Dimon's 'dumb things' remark frames the private-credit debate, and FS KKR's private-credit fund cut its dividend. HYG closed at 80.85, down 0.23% over 20 sessions, while LQD closed at 111.72, up 0.97% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-26). The institutional response is to build products: State Street expanded its actively managed corporate-bond fund range, even as the default warnings grow.

Equity & Fund Flows: Private equity is targeting IPO escape velocity on AI winners, and Plaid's $8 billion valuation shows private marks rising for some names. Man Group's shares fell as its profits declined even though its assets hit a record. Retail is buying the dip: small investors bought Nvidia in record numbers after the open. Buybacks are contested: Salesforce's $50 billion plan is proving controversial on Wall Street. Hedge-fund personnel are moving: Millennium poached Goldman's equities co-chief, and Hudson Bay's husband-and-wife trading duo in Dubai is exiting for Dymon.

Portfolio Implication: Mixed. Keep equity beta, but hedge credit by buying high-yield protection and staying in investment grade rather than high yield. Prefer duration while the curve bull-flattens and the 10Y is 4.02%. Keep a dollar hedge for emerging-market exposure, because reserve managers are trimming the dollar. The signal to cut risk is HYG closing below its 80.85 level. The emerging-market read is constructive on flows: the Philippine peso is on track for its best start in 14 years, and the dollar-weakness trade is what feeds it. The risk is that the same weak dollar reverses if the tariff path turns.

What Is Priced: The US is keeping China tariffs steady ahead of a key Trump–Xi meeting, according to Greer, and China has received a major reprieve on tariffs without a reversal being expected. The yuan keeps advancing after the PBOC set another stronger fixing, while Beijing tries to slow the gains. Pending: the Trump–Xi meeting itself, with the tariff level held in place until then.

Conditional Expression: If the meeting delivers, the trade is long A-share exposure through ASHR, up 1.52% over 20 sessions at 34.17, and long the yuan. If it stalls, buy protection on KWEB, which is down 12.83% over 20 sessions at 31.46, and unwind the currency carry. The rule is that the summit outcome sets the direction, not the tariff headline.

Risk: Beijing's export controls are coming of age as Trump reins in tech curbs, and Nvidia has still not sold its US-approved China AI chips. A summit can freeze chip sales even as tariffs hold, so the tariff settlement is not the same as a tech settlement. Beijing's own tariff countermeasures are still to be decided 'in due course', so Beijing keeps a retaliation option open.

What Is Priced: The odds of early cuts under a Warsh-led Fed have slid, Goolsbee sees several more cuts this year but not soon, and Miran still sees four quarter-point cuts. Pending: the Fed's challenge to Justice Department subpoenas, which adds a governance question to the rate path.

Conditional Expression: If early cuts stay off the table, the 10Y stays near 4.02% and the curve keeps bull-flattening, so trade the front end at 3.42% for carry. If a dovish chair brings a 2026 cut back into focus, own duration through TLT, up 3.05% over 20 sessions, and the rate-sensitive housing names, where XLRE is up 6.81%.

Risk: Fiscal supply is the offset. The CBO sees the deficit reaching 5.9% of GDP by 2030, and the IMF says the US should shift gears on economic policy. Heavier issuance could steepen the curve despite a Fed that cuts. The fiscal and political backdrop is changing too, with Japan also planning an aid programme for the so-called ice-age generation by March.

What Is Priced: The BOJ has left the door open to near-term hikes and signalled data-driven hikes, while the government picked reflationists for the board. USD/JPY closed at 156.2000, up 2.03% over 20 sessions, and the finance minister is vigilant on yen weakness.

Conditional Expression: If the BOJ hikes in the spring as signalled, the trade is long yen against the dollar, with a stop above the 156.2000 close. If it holds with a dovish board majority, buy USD/JPY calls and hedge with Nikkei exposure, since the index is at a record high.

Risk: Core inflation in Tokyo is slowing below the BOJ's 2% target, which gives the doves an argument. A hike that is not followed by more hikes would leave the yen to the politics rather than the policy.

What Is Priced: Oil settled down after a choppy session as traders followed the US–Iran talks, and gold is steady as markets await the nuclear talks outcome. The Middle East is bracing for another conflict, but uncertainty remains over Trump's final decision, and the top US commander briefed Trump on Iran options. Pending: US–Venezuela oil sales expected to reach $2 billion by the end of February.

Conditional Expression: If talks produce a deal, the premium leaves Brent, which is at 70.75 and down 1.27% over five sessions, and XLE, up 9.99% over 20 sessions, gives back first. If strikes follow, the trade is long oil through USO at 79.77 with gold (5,194.20) as the hedge.

Risk: Venezuelan barrels are a supply offset: Eni can now receive oil from Venezuela as payment for gas, and a Forbes analysis says the US takeover of Venezuelan oil will not move the global market. A glut can outweigh a geopolitical premium even if the talks fail. A separate geopolitical risk runs through the Geneva talks: Ukraine and the US began talks in Geneva, and Russia launched major strikes before them.

Catalyst & Thesis: Nvidia's record quarter produced $43 billion of quarterly profit, and the company expects its gaming-chip shortage to last until year-end. The stock sank 5% anyway, because investors fretted over returns and wanted more cash return. Thesis: the fundamental run continues, but the stock needs a capital-return answer before the multiple re-rates.

Price Hurdle & Risk: NVDA closed at 184.89 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-26), down 5.46% in the prior session and 3.46% over 20 sessions. Risk: Congress is taking on Nvidia and the White House as it pushes for chip export limits, which would be a direct hit to the China-linked upside.

Trade Expression: Buy shares or a three-month call spread into the next capital-return headline, sized for further pressure. Invalidation: a cash-return announcement that does not come, or export limits that pass into law.

Catalyst & Thesis: The smartphone market is set to shrink 13% in 2026 on the memory chip crisis, IDC says, and the decline is the biggest ever, on a memory price surge. Micron is up 326% in a year. Thesis: memory pricing is the margin driver for the supplier, while the device makers' volume loss is the warning.

Price Hurdle & Risk: MU closed at 415.56 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-26), down 3.13% in the prior session and 4.53% over 20 sessions. Risk: device demand falls faster than memory prices rise, which would turn the supplier's pricing power into a volume problem.

Trade Expression: Long shares on weakness, sized for a sharp move in either direction. Invalidation: device shipments falling faster than the memory price rise, or a contract price roll-over, both of which would show before Micron's guidance does.

Catalyst & Thesis: ASML says its next-generation EUV tools are ready to mass-produce chips, and a headline says its latest EUV breakthrough puts would-be rivals further behind. Thesis: the tool is the capacity constraint for the AI chip cycle, so a ready product lifts the multiple even when the day's tape is weak.

Price Hurdle & Risk: ASML closed at 1,463.80 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-26), down 4.11% in the prior session and up 2.87% over 20 sessions. The day's sell-off is the hurdle: a headline says ASML was down on the day. Risk: US export limits on chips, which Congress is pushing.

Trade Expression: Buy the shares on weakness, or the semiconductor ETF SOXX at 356.80, down 1.02% over 20 sessions. Invalidation: export controls tightened on lithography, or a capex cut from the largest cloud buyers.

Catalyst & Thesis: The White House is hosting Big Tech after a pledge to rein in power costs, and Texas approved a data-centre behemoth's gas power play. Thesis: generators are the paid party in the data-centre power pledge, but the pledge is still unclear on what it commits.

Price Hurdle & Risk: CEG closed at 323.56 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-26), down 0.70% in the prior session, up 12.37% over 20 sessions and 10.94% over five sessions. The price already prices much of the pledge. Risk: Georgia's Senate blocked a vote on a data-centre energy bill, a sign that state rules may be slower than the federal headline.

Trade Expression: Hold the position and do not add above the card close. Protect the gain with a put spread. Invalidation: a bring-your-own-power contract that carries no price terms, or a state-level block that spreads.

Catalyst & Thesis: Stellantis posted its first annual loss in company history after EV write-downs, and a €22 billion loss came with higher US tariff costs. The US closed its probe into 7.4 million vehicles without seeking a recall, but the company is weighing Chinese EV technology for Europe. Thesis: the profit-rebound promise has a cost that is still being set.

Price Hurdle & Risk: STLA closed at 8.05 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-26), up 4.41% in the prior session but down 17.01% over 20 sessions. The stock rose despite the loss, which means the bear case has to be on earnings revisions rather than the tape.

Trade Expression: Underweight the name against the European auto tracker, or a put spread into the next earnings print. Invalidation: a clean profit-rebound plan with no China tech deal, or a sales beat that the market rewards.

Catalyst & Thesis: Meta signed a multi-billion-dollar deal to rent Google's AI chips. Thesis: the compute shortage is real, so platform companies with cash will keep buying capacity, even from rivals, and the rental deal confirms the demand line.

Price Hurdle & Risk: META closed at 657.01 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-26), up 0.51% in the prior session and down 1.75% over 20 sessions. Risk: the capex bill grows faster than the revenue line, and the market responds to capex with a lower multiple.

Trade Expression: Buy the shares on a pullback toward the 20-session level, or a call spread into the next capex update. Invalidation: a capex cut from the platform's own plan, or a rental deal that is not extended.

Observed Attention: The Motley Fool asks whether Reddit is a buy after a 35% fall this year, and a headline says Reddit traders are getting cold feet even as Merck's stock jumps. The card has no Reddit price, so there is no hurdle to test.

Motivation & Bias: Retail is treating a 35% drawdown as a buying opportunity, and the forum bias is to read the cold feet as a contrarian sign. Reddit's own traders are the audience, so the signal is more about the crowd than the stock.
Instrument & Risk: Shares only, sized for a gap. Any entry needs its own reference point, because the card gives no RDDT close.

Observed Attention: A CNBC headline says small investors bought Nvidia in record numbers after Thursday's open, after the stock sank 5% on the results. The card has NVDA at 184.89, down 5.46% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-26).

Motivation & Bias: Small investors are buying the dip on the earnings beat, and the bias is to read the sell-off as an entry. The Breakingviews commentary that Nvidia is dogged by memories of cycles past is the counterweight.
Instrument & Risk: Shares or short-dated calls. The risk is a second leg down if export limits pass, which would hit the buy-the-dip crowd first.

Observed Attention: Circle is nearly 50% higher in two sessions since its earnings, a CoinDesk headline says. Its earnings had already lifted the shares, and the retail chase has followed the stablecoin story rather than the fundamentals.

Motivation & Bias: Retail is buying the stablecoin narrative after a sharp move, which is a recency bias. The stablecoin-model caution in the GENIUS coverage is the bear case that the momentum crowd tends to ignore.
Instrument & Risk: Shares only. The card has no CRCL close, so the risk is a reversal of the two-session move, which can be sharp.

Observed Attention: A FXEmpire headline says COMEX tightness supports a bullish silver outlook. The card has SLV at 80.45, up 13.29% over five sessions and down 23.82% over 20 sessions, and silver futures at 87.00, down 23.09% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-26).
Motivation & Bias: Retail is chasing the five-session bounce after a 20-session crash. The bias is recency: the rebound is the thing being bought, not the drawdown that preceded it.
Instrument & Risk: SLV or silver futures. The moves are violent in both directions, and the 20-session fall means a reversal of the bounce can erase it quickly.

Market data: Yahoo Finance, prior completed sessions; Treasury curve: US Treasury daily par yields. Changes are price changes, not total returns. Currency sessions follow exchange-local dates; crypto observations include weekends.
